title: Smart Batch Orchestrator: workload signatures, safety guards, and continuous window tuning
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a Smart Batch Orchestrator (SBO) that continuously recommends and safely applies batching and caching parameters per workload. SBO will profile live traffic to infer 'workload signatures' (inference footprint distribution, token length histograms, client concurrency patterns, and prompt prefix commonalities) and produce a ranked set of parameter changes (batch size, aggregation window, token-threshold, aggressive KV cache retention) together with an estimated cost delta and latency risk. The ticket covers design and a first-pass implementation for: (1) offline profiling + feature extraction, (2) a heuristic recommender that maps signatures to parameter candidates, (3) safe-apply primitives (canary split, dry-run simulation, rollback triggers), and (4) Console UI hooks for review and acceptance. The goal is automated, conservative recommendations that reduce per-token cost without violating latency SLOs or increasing tail errors.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SBO generates candidate parameter sets for at least three distinct workload signatures in staging; 2) Each recommendation includes numeric estimates for expected token-cost delta, 95th/99th latency impact, and confidence score; 3) Safe-apply flow executes a canary (5% traffic) and rolls back automatically if 95th latency increases by >10% or error-rate >1% absolute; 4) Console displays recommendations with links to profiling artifact and simulation run for operator review; 5) End-to-end tests for dry-run simulation, canary steering, and automated rollback are green in CI.
design_notes: Workload signatures: derive a compact vector composed of median and p90 input token counts, per-client QPS quantiles, prompt prefix entropy (hash buckets), and observed KV cache hit-rate. Heuristics: map signature clusters to parameter families using rules (e.g., low-latency/high-QPS -> smaller continuous window + aggressive batching; high-variance long prompts -> larger per-request token-threshold but reduced aggregation window). Confidence model: estimate based on similarity to canonical clusters and recent stability of traffic. Safety guards: dry-run simulator (replay sampled live requests against candidate params in echo mode, measure simulated latencies and cache-hit deltas), canary controller with phased ramp, circuit-breaker thresholds derived from baseline SLOs. Metrics to track: cost-per-100k-tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, KV cache hit-rate, model throughput, queue length. Implementation will live in runtime/orchestrator service and expose an API endpoint for Console to fetch recommendations.
implementation_steps: 1) Instrumentation: add lightweight per-request sampling (0.5-1%) to collect token counts, client id, latency breakdowns, and KV cache events; 2) Offline profiler: batch collected samples hourly into feature vectors and cluster signatures using k-means (k tunable); 3) Heuristic mapping: author initial rule set for parameter families and encode as ordered rules that fall back to safe defaults; 4) Simulator: build request replayer that runs sampled requests through current runtime with proposed params in a sandbox mode (no external side effects) and emits delta metrics; 5) Safe-apply controller: implement canary split, phased ramping with automated rollback hooks and change audit log; 6) Console integration: UI for recommendation list, simulation artifacts, and one-click apply/rollback; 7) E2E tests and load tests in staging; 8) Pilot on non-critical customer tenants for 2 weeks before broader rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misapplied batching increases tail latency and degrades UX. Mitigation: conservative defaults, low initial canary traffic (5%), strict rollback thresholds, dry-run simulation before apply. Risk: signatures drift faster than profiling cadence causing stale recommendations. Mitigation: add sliding-window recency weight and surface staleness warnings in Console. Risk: privacy concerns from sampling client ids. Mitigation: hash client ids with server salt and only store hash buckets; retain only aggregated stats beyond 7 days.
notes: We examined prior artifacts: autotune experiments and the adaptive-batching recommender prototypes. This ticket intentionally focuses on conservative heuristics and safety-first apply semantics rather than ML-only actions. Long-term plan: replace heuristics with a learned policy once robust reward signals and offline evaluation harnesses exist.
